the vibrational relaxation rate coefficients k10 of NO in Ar are well above the Landau-Teller predictions and that this is due to tunneling in the curve-crossing mechanism of the NO-Ar system.

the vibrational relaxation of the NO molecule in collisions with Ar atoms is strongly affected by tunneling of the collision complex through a curve-crossing barrier in the (A'', A') potential energy surface.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new mechanism for vibrational relaxation of polyatomic molecules, namely, tunneling in a nonadiabatic mechanism.
a curve-crossing model of vibrational energy transfer in a diatom-diatom collision system, in which the tunneling effect is important at low temperatures.
a new class of nonadiabatic processes, namely, the tunneling in curve-crossing transitions of diabatic states.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NO-Ar relaxation data are well described by the Landau-Teller mechanism for high temperatures and by tunneling-assisted curve-crossing for intermediate and low temperatures.
the NO-Ar vibrational relaxation is dominated by nonadiabatic tunneling at all temperatures.

the vibrational relaxation of excited NO(X, v = 2) in collisions with Ar is dominated by the Landau-Teller mechanism, whereas the relaxation of NO(X, v > 2) proceeds mainly via a curve-crossing (LZ) mechanism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the measured k10 can be described as the sum of two contributions: (i) an adiabatic (LZ)10 and a nonadiabatic (LZA)10 term, which can be described by the effective mass model, and (ii) a nonadiabatically induced tunneling term (LT)10, which can be estimated by the linear model and the Landau-Lfshitz WKB approximation.

the tunneling contribution to the nonadi-abatic curve-crossing mechanism is significant over a broad temperature range, which may also be relevant to the vibrational relaxation of other small molecules in rare gas collisions.
the vibrational relaxation of the NO(X(2))Π, v =1) state in Ar can be well described by the Landau-Zener model at high temperatures (T > 900 K).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the tunneling effect in the curve-crossing relaxation of NO-Ar is very pronounced and should be taken into account in future theoretical treatments of the NO-Ar system.
the nonadiabatically enhanced vibrational relaxation of a molecule can be very efficient at low temperatures.
tunneling can play a significant role in the nonadiabatically mediated vibrational relaxation of molecules in rare gas environments.
